problem:
The amount of a rare plant species $A(t)$ after $t$ years can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=0.072A.
$$

If there are currently $320$ plants, calculate the amount after $9$ years. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

The amount of the plant species after $9$ years is approximately 
{{field-1}}
plants.
worked_solution:
We model the amount using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=0.072A.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
A(t)={A}_{0}\,{e}^{0.072t},
$$

where ${A}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there are currently $320$ plants, so we have ${A}_{0}=320.$

Therefore, the amount $A$ at time $t$ is

$$
A(t)=320\,{e}^{0.072t}.
$$

Finally, to find the amount when $t=9,$ we substitute $t=9$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A(9) & =320\,{e}^{0.072\cdot 9} \\  & =320\,{e}^{0.648} \\  & ≈611.53\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that the amount of the plant species after $9$ years is approximately $612$ plants.
